REST API / Using the REST API / Best practices

Best practices for using the REST API

This guide covers consuming GitHub's REST API, rather than designing a general REST API.

Prefer events to repeated reads

Use webhooks instead of polling the API. Subscribe to the events your integration needs and process each delivery.

Authenticate requests

Make authenticated requests to obtain the appropriate rate limit. Keep credentials secret and grant only the permissions required by your integration.

Avoid concurrent requests

Send requests serially to reduce the risk of secondary rate limits. Pause between large numbers of mutating requests.

Handle rate limit responses

Respect Retry-After when the server returns it. Wait for the rate limit reset when the remaining quota is zero.

Response headerClient action
Retry-AfterWait the specified number of seconds before another request.
x-ratelimit-resetResume after the reset time when the quota is exhausted.

Use conditional requests

Cache the ETag response value and send it in If-None-Match on subsequent requests.

curl --header 'If-None-Match: "cached-etag"' https://api.github.com/repos/example/project
A 304 response can reuse the cached representation.

Follow published URLs

Follow pagination links supplied in the Link response header. Do not parse identifiers out of URLs or assume undocumented URL shapes remain stable.
